subject: POC acceptance criteria & recommended model pair for trial
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Asha Nair <asha@polaris.ai>
Cc: Jonah Keene <jonah.keene@polaris.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + PoC acceptance criteria, timeline, and next steps

Hi Asha / Jonah,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on the immediate objectives. Per our discussion, I put together a concise PoC charter and acceptance criteria so we can lock timelines and owners. Please review and let me know any edits; I attached the editable checklist.

High-level goal:
- Validate Redwood inference for clinical triage summarization at 200-400 reqs/min with accurate Spanish/English outputs and <500ms 95th pct token latency under the dedicated trial profile.

Success criteria (must pass at least 3 of 4):
- Precision on triage label extraction >= 88% (measured over 1,200 annotated cases)
- Multilingual fidelity: Spanish and Portuguese macro-F1 >= 0.85 on subset tests
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency <= 500ms on reserved capacity during 30m sustained window
- Cost: per-token inference cost <= target in PoC budget (we'll surface exact numbers after capacity reservation)

Scope & timelines:
- Kickoff & dataset handoff: Week of Aug 16 (you to provide sample dataset + labeling spec)
- Baseline runs (3 model variants): Aug 17–21
- Eval + shortlisting: Aug 24–28
- PoC validation run (72-hour sustained): Sep 1–3
- Final review + decision: Sep 7

Ownership:
- Polaris: sample dataset, annotation guideline, primary reviewers (Asha / Jonah)
- Redwood: experiment setup, baseline evaluation, monitoring dashboards, canary routing for failover (Sergio)
- CS/Eng ops: test harness, cost reporting (Marissa Cole)

Model recommendations for trial (initial shortlist):
1) Mistral-Instruct-7B (primary) — good tradeoff for instruction tuning, low memory for our dedicated pools
2) Llama-2-13b-chat (fallback high-quality) — use quantized q4_0 for cost control; test for hallucination on clinical data
3) Falcon-7B-Instruct (multilingual candidate) — lighter and fast on subword variants; good Spanish baseline

Multilingual notes:
- We should evaluate the tokenizer mismatch across Spanish and Portuguese content early. Suggest a 200-sentence per-language prompt test for tokenization drift and output length variance.

Attachments: PoC-Checklist.xlsx (editable) — please accept the checklist and confirm dataset delivery date.

Next steps (action items):
- Asha: confirm sample dataset delivery date (owner)
- Jonah: confirm procurement timeline for SOW and any contracting constraints
- Marissa: follow up on capacity pricing and whether a short reserved burst is acceptable for the 72hr run
- Sergio: schedule kickoff once dataset ETA confirmed

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the clear summary — this aligns with our internal expectations. A few clarifications:
- We can provide a ~1.5k row sample dataset by Aug 18. Final annotated set will be ready Sep 1 if the SOW is signed this week.
- Procurement: Jonah will shepherd the SOW; typical turnaround is 7–10 business days.
- On success criteria: we might need to relax the latency target to 600ms 95th initially (our infra baseline is higher), but we'll prioritize model correctness first.

We've signed the NDA (attached) so you should have the PDF on file.

Asha
VP Product, Polaris HealthTech
asha@polaris.ai

Subject: Re: Recap + PoC acceptance criteria, timeline, and next steps

Thanks for looping me in — noted. A few internal items / model rationale from the Optimize + EngOps side: 

1) Pricing & capacity
- For the 72-hour validation window we'll recommend a short reserved capacity allocation (2 gpus equivalent) and a burst policy. I'll confirm exact monthlyized cost and a short-term commit option by EOD Thursday.

2) Model pairing recommendation (production-like roster)
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (user-facing baseline) — lower memory, fast infer, good instruction-following.
- Quality candidate: Llama-2-13b-chat (q4_0 quant) — tradeoff is memory but better for edge-case extraction; we'll test hallucination risk on the clinical subset.
- Fallback: Falcon-7B-Instruct (or a trimmed Falcon quant) — configured behind smart routing with 3-way fallbacks for high latency / quality regressions.

3) Multilingual strategy
- Run tokenization and perplexity checks per language. If Spanish/Portuguese show consistent degradation vs. English we should add a small language-specific prompt template and eval set.

4) Experiment matrix (what we'll deliver)
- Baseline metrics CSV (per model): latency, tokens/sec, cost/token estimate, recall/precision by label, multilingual F1
- Shortlist recommendation and a single canonical model variant to move into traffic if pass thresholds

I attached a quick model-selection matrix (CSV) with initial perf assumptions. Dylan / Evelyn — can you take the ownership on the baseline runs (Aug 17–21)? Sergio, I'll sync pricing with you separately.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Model-Selection-Matrix.csv
